name: Brute Force
description: Adversaries systematically guess or crack credentials to gain access to accounts when passwords are unknown or only hashes are available.

name: Password Guessing
description: Trying common or likely passwords against one account or a small set of accounts.

name: Password Cracking
description: Recovering plaintext passwords offline from stolen password hashes.

name: Password Spraying
description: Trying one or a few common passwords against many accounts to stay under account lockout thresholds.

name: Credential Stuffing
description: Reusing username and password pairs leaked from breaches of unrelated services.

name: Phishing
description: Sending deceptive electronic messages to trick victims into running code, opening links or giving up credentials.

name: Spearphishing Attachment
description: Targeted phishing messages that carry a malicious file attachment.

name: Spearphishing Link
description: Targeted phishing messages that contain a malicious link.

name: Spearphishing via Service
description: Phishing through third-party services such as social media or personal webmail instead of corporate email.

name: Spearphishing Voice
description: Phone-based phishing (vishing) to obtain credentials, MFA approvals or remote access.

name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
description: Abusing built-in command and script interpreters to execute commands, scripts or binaries.

name: PowerShell
description: Abusing PowerShell, often with encoded commands or in-memory download cradles.

name: Windows Command Shell
description: Abusing cmd.exe and batch scripts to execute commands.

name: Unix Shell
description: Abusing sh, bash or zsh on Linux and macOS to execute commands.

name: Data Encrypted for Impact
description: Encrypting data on systems or across a network to disrupt availability, typically ransomware.

name: Inhibit System Recovery
description: Deleting backups, shadow copies or recovery features so victims cannot restore systems.

name: Service Stop
description: Stopping or disabling services, for example databases or backups, to make systems or data unavailable.

name: Valid Accounts
tactic: Defense Evasion, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, Initial Access
description: Using credentials of existing accounts to gain access, persist and evade defenses.

name: OS Credential Dumping
description: Extracting credential material such as password hashes from the operating system, for example from LSASS memory.

name: Remote Services
description: Using valid accounts to log into remote services such as RDP, SSH or SMB to move between systems.
